about: Campaign Mode's inbox (docs/CAMPAIGN-MODE.md section 12): messages arrive on their week and expire at that week's End Week. Each option shows the You get / It costs / Risk preview; 'meeting' books a slot (public, semi or shadow venue) and happens at End Week; 'fail' is a hidden chance; 'trace' a hidden trace weight; 'dirty' counts as dark play. Venues are invented, or public landmarks.

messages.label: Verified
messages.subject: Where do you stand on the rent cap bill?
messages.body: Rosa Ferreira, Astoria Tenants' Alliance: "Four thousand tenants want to know if {candidate} backs the rent cap bill. We vote as a block. A big one."

options.label: Promise to back it
options.cost: A promise you'll be held to
options.receipt: Rosa's members cheered. Developers sharpened their pencils.

fail.receipt: Rosa's members cheered, and a developer pulled a C$3,000 pledge.

options.label: Say you're "studying it"
options.receipt: "Studying it." Rosa has heard that one before.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.receipt: A developer sent a C$2,000 thank-you. Rosa sent a strongly worded flyer.

messages.label: Verified
messages.subject: Dinner Thursday at the Olympia Diner
messages.body: Gus Papadakis, Ditmars Merchants' Association: "Thursday, 8pm, the corner booth. Bring {candidate}'s appetite and your pollster. The shop owners on Ditmars want to meet the person who wants their windows."

options.label: Go, with your pollster
options.get: Shop windows for posters, a Favor
options.receipt: Gus fed everyone and promised posters in forty windows. A Favor owed.

options.label: Send Sol instead
options.receipt: Sol ate the moussaka and got twelve windows. Gus asked where you were.

options.label: Decline
options.receipt: Gus said "no problem" in the voice that means problem.

messages.label: Anonymous
messages.subject: A gift, no strings (some strings)
messages.body: "A friend of the campaign would like to help. C$20,000 in cash, delivered in a gym bag. He'll call in a small favor later. Nothing illegal. Mostly."

options.label: Take the bag
options.receipt: C$20,000 in a gym bag. It smells like a gym bag.

options.label: Decline
options.receipt: You said no. Your deputy said nothing, loudly.

options.label: Tell a reporter
options.receipt: The Borough Bugle ran "Campaign Turns Down Mystery Gym Bag." +1.

messages.label: Unverified
messages.subject: Ever wonder what ribbons cost?
messages.body: Marguerite Lin, The Borough Bugle: "I'm told City Hall spent more on ceremonial ribbon this year than on bus shelters. I need one more source. Coffee?"

options.label: Meet her for coffee
options.get: Intel on the Mayor, a story
options.receipt: Lin's ribbon story ran. The Mayor is now photographed with scissors less often.

options.label: Trade it for a friendly profile
options.receipt: A glowing profile of {candidate} ran the same week. Coincidence, says everyone.

options.label: Ignore it
options.receipt: You let it go. Lin found another source.

messages.label: Verified
messages.subject: About your housing plan
messages.body: Harlan Pryce, Pryce Development: "I like {candidate}. I like towers more. Soften the housing talk, or my checks start going to City Hall."

options.label: Soften the housing talk
options.receipt: Pryce's C$8,000 arrived. So did a tenants' flyer with your face on it.

options.label: Call his bluff
options.receipt: Pryce blinked. He also stopped returning calls.

fail.receipt: Pryce wasn't bluffing. His money went to the Mayor's machine.

options.label: Offer him a seat on a "housing panel"
options.receipt: Pryce loves a panel. He'll keep writing checks for now.

messages.label: Anonymous
messages.subject: 50,000 followers by Friday
messages.body: "We run accounts. Lots of accounts. C$4,000 and {candidate} trends by the weekend. Real people, mostly."

options.label: Buy the bot push
options.receipt: {candidate} trended. Several of the fans have no faces.

fail.receipt: The bots got flagged in a day. "Bot-gate" trended instead. -1.

options.label: Delete the message
options.receipt: Deleted. The internet stays exactly as fake as it was.

messages.label: Anonymous
messages.subject: Under the Hell Gate Bridge, 11pm
messages.body: "I work for the Mayor. I'm tired. I have his debate notes. Come alone."

options.label: Go
options.receipt: A nervous aide, a damp envelope, the Mayor's debate notes. Attack will land.

fail.receipt: Nobody came. Someone took a photo of you waiting under a bridge at 11pm.

options.label: Send a cut-out
options.receipt: Your cut-out came back with half the notes and a cold.

options.label: Report it
options.receipt: You reported it. The Mayor's office sent a thank-you card. With a ribbon.

messages.label: Verified
messages.subject: Speak at the urban futures colloquium
messages.body: Dean Samir Haddad, St. Johnsons University: "Our students would love to hear {candidate}'s plan for the city. There will be a Q&A. They ask hard questions. They've been practicing."

options.label: Accept
options.receipt: The students grilled {candidate}. It was great practice. A Favor from the dean.

options.label: Decline
options.receipt: The dean said he understood. He wrote it down.

messages.label: Verified
messages.subject: 4am last call, yes or no?
messages.body: Jojo Reyes, nightlife promoter: "Every club in Astoria wants to know: will {candidate} back 4am last call? I can put your face on every bathroom mirror in Queens."

options.label: Back 4am last call
options.receipt: Your face is on every bathroom mirror in Astoria. The night owls are in.

options.label: "Let's talk after the election"
options.receipt: Jojo left you on read.

options.label: Say no
options.receipt: Jojo booked a DJ to play your concession speech. Early.

messages.label: Verified
messages.subject: Sign our letter on transit wages
messages.body: Deb Okonkwo, President of Local 117: "Sign our letter for a transit worker raise and our members knock doors for you all week. Don't, and they knock for somebody else."

options.label: Sign it
options.receipt: Local 117 hit the streets in matching jackets. A donor hit unsubscribe.

options.label: Sign a softer version
options.receipt: Deb took the soft letter. Her members knocked on about half the doors.

options.label: Decline
options.receipt: Local 117 knocked doors for the Mayor. He brought them donuts. With ribbons.

messages.label: Verified
messages.subject: Sunday breakfast in Jamaica
messages.body: Pastor Ellis Grant, Greater Jamaica Fellowship: "Two hundred neighbors, eggs and coffee, and a microphone. No speeches longer than the grits stay warm."

options.label: Go
options.receipt: {candidate} kept it short. The grits stayed warm. Jamaica noticed.

options.label: Decline
options.receipt: The Mayor went instead. He cut a ribbon on the coffee urn.

messages.label: Anonymous
messages.subject: The ribbon man wants a word
messages.body: "Teddy Vance here. I sell City Hall its ribbons. Forty years. If {candidate} wins, will they still need ribbons? Asking for a business."

options.label: Promise him the ribbon contract
options.receipt: Teddy switched sides with a C$5,000 check and a lifetime supply of ribbon.

options.label: Tell him the truth: fewer ribbons
options.receipt: Teddy said he respected the honesty. Then ordered more ribbon for the Mayor.
